explanations.explanation: This neuron is basically a “common‐subword” detector.  It lights up on very short, high-frequency BPE pieces or punctuation (e.g. “hopes”, “too”, “as”, “ur”, left/right quotes, etc.) and is strongly negative on longer, rarer tokens (proper names, long words, uncommon subwords).

This neuron detects orthographic markers of proper-name subwords—foreign diacritics (ú, ñ, etc.), uppercase onsets after hyphens or ampersands (e.g. S & P, B & B, Mosi-oa-Tunya), and other non-ASCII or special‐character cues that typically signal parts of names, brands, places or indices.
